questions.q: Which deployment option does Microsoft recommend as the default for Foundry Models?
options: Managed compute
Serverless API endpoint
Standard deployment in a Foundry resource
There is no recommended default
questions.explain: Microsoft recommends standard deployment in a Foundry resource as the default, since it offers the widest range of capabilities among the three options.

questions.q: What is required before you can deploy a model from a partner provider like Cohere for the first time in a project?
options: Nothing extra — all models deploy identically
A subscription to the model's offering through Azure Marketplace
A support ticket with Microsoft
Writing custom deployment code
questions.explain: Models from partners and community route through Azure Marketplace. You subscribe to the specific model's offering once per project before deploying it the first time.

questions.q: What is true about content filtering across the three deployment options?
options: It's enabled by default on all three options
It's never available on any deployment option
It's available on Foundry resources and serverless API, but not managed compute
It can only be enabled through a support request
questions.explain: Content filtering ships with Foundry resource and serverless API deployments, but managed compute deployments do not support it.

questions.q: Which deployment option is billed by compute core-hours rather than tokens?
options: Standard deployment in a Foundry resource
Serverless API endpoint
Managed compute
All three are billed identically
questions.explain: Managed compute is billed per compute core-hour, based on the VM size and instance count, rather than by tokens processed.

questions.q: Which capability is unique to standard deployment in a Foundry resource, among the three options?
options: Keyless authentication with Microsoft Entra ID
The ability to run inference at all
Support for text-based models only
Free, unlimited usage
questions.explain: Keyless authentication through Microsoft Entra ID is only available on standard deployments in a Foundry resource — serverless and managed compute both require key-based authentication.
